<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919272_theRebbe_883" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919272_theRebbe_883__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the great descent of the soul into this lowly world, which is ultimately for the purpose of an ascent to a level higher than before its descent, even to Atzmus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand this more particularly,</t>
    <t s="2">we must first preface the general matter of the descent of the soul below, which is a great descent from a high roof to a deep pit.</t>
    <t s="3">For the soul, before its descent below, is pure,</t>
    <t s="4">and there are several explanations of this,</t>
    <t s="5">One: that it refers to the World of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="6">Two: the lower purity (Tahiru Tata’ah),</t>
    <t s="7">Three: the upper purity (Tahiru Ila’ah).</t>
    <t s="8">And its descent is to the very lowest,</t>
    <t s="9">not only to the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="10">the worlds of separation in general,</t>
    <t s="11">but rather to this lowly world, below which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="12">most of which is evil, with only a little good mixed within it,</t>
    <t s="13">to the extent that the deeds of this world are harsh, etc.</t>
    <t s="14">(as explained in Tanya</t>
    <t s="15">in the name of the Etz Chaim),</t>
    <t s="16">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="17">the service in this world itself is in the very lowest place,</t>
    <t s="18">in the place of “for you descended to Egypt” and in the manner of “the evil inclination is among you,”</t>
    <t s="19">requiring one to wage war with the evil inclination, as “today it says to him ‘do this,’ and tomorrow ‘serve idols,’”</t>
    <t s="20">which is the opposite of “I am the L-rd your G-d” and “You shall have no other gods”</t>
    <t s="21">(the root of the 248 positive commandments and 365 negative commandments,</t>
    <t s="22">as explained in Tanya),</t>
    <t s="23">However, this descent is for the purpose of an ascent.</t>
    <t s="24">For even though the soul did not descend to rectify itself, etc., but rather to rectify its body, its animal soul, and its portion in the world</t>
    <t s="25">(as explained in Etz Chaim,</t>
    <t s="26">cited in Tanya),</t>
    <t s="27">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="28">through the descent of the soul below, it is elevated to a level higher than it was before its descent,</t>
    <t s="29">above even the World of Emanation.</t>
    <t s="30">And even more,</t>
    <t s="31">to a level that has no comparison or connection to the matter of Hishtalshelus (order of descent), level, or rank,</t>
    <t s="32">to the extent that it is not even possible to say that it has a level relative to the order of Hishtalshelus,</t>
    <t s="33">but only in the known expression,</t>
    <t s="34">“to be absorbed in the body of the King,”</t>
    <t s="35">in His Essence and Being, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="36">And in the language of the Zohar elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="37">in this level, “they are not found in the King except for Yisrael alone”</t>
    <t s="38">(which is above even Torah and Mitzvos).</t>
    <t s="39">And the ascent is through service in Torah and Mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="40">for “I was created only to serve my Master,”</t>
    <t s="41">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="42">“And He placed him… to work it and to guard it,”</t>
    <t s="43">“to work it” refers to the 248 positive commandments, and “to guard it” refers to the 365 negative commandments</t>
    <t s="44">(for wherever it says “guard,” etc., it is only a negative commandment),</t>
    <t s="45">and this requires the preface of the Torah that “study is greater, for it brings to action.”</t>
    <t s="46">And also, conquering the evil inclination is through the Torah, as our sages said,</t>
    <t s="47">“I created the evil inclination, and I created the Torah as its spice,”</t>
    <t s="48">and “if this abomination meets you, drag it to the study hall,” etc.</t>
    <t s="49">And this is what is written,</t>
    <t s="50">“Turn from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it,”</t>
    <t s="51">which refers to positive commandments, negative commandments, and Torah,</t>
    <t s="52">as explained in Likkutei Torah on our portion</t>
    <t s="53">(Balak).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the soul’s ascent to a level incomparably higher than before is specifically through its work below, because it refines the lofty sparks from the World of Tohu that fell lower.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">However, we need to understand the reason for the matter,</t>
    <t s="2">that specifically through the service of the soul below it is elevated to a level higher than it was before its descent,</t>
    <t s="3">even to an ascent that is incomparable to its previous level.</t>
    <t s="4">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="5">that the sparks within physical matters have their source in the World of Tohu, which is above the World of Tikkun.</t>
    <t s="6">And as it is written,</t>
    <t s="7">“For not by bread alone does man live, but by every utterance of the mouth of G-d does man live.”</t>
    <t s="8">And the Arizal explains,</t>
    <t s="9">that “the utterance of the mouth of G-d” in the bread is the G-dly spark within it.</t>
    <t s="10">And even though there is also within man an “utterance of the mouth of G-d” that gives him life,</t>
    <t s="11">nevertheless, he specifically needs the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” that is in the bread,</t>
    <t s="12">for whatever is higher falls lower.</t>
    <t s="13">And it is like the parable of a stone at the top of a wall,</t>
    <t s="14">when it falls down, it falls farther from the wall than a stone that falls from the middle of the wall, etc.</t>
    <t s="15">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="16">since the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” in the bread fell lower than the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” in man,</t>
    <t s="17">for bread is from the vegetative realm,</t>
    <t s="18">and especially at the time of eating it is no longer vegetative but rather inanimate</t>
    <t s="19">(and furthermore,</t>
    <t s="20">eating bread is with salt,</t>
    <t s="21">which is inanimate),</t>
    <t s="22">while man is a speaker,</t>
    <t s="23">this itself is proof that the source of the sparks found in the bread is higher than the “utterance of the mouth of G-d” in man,</t>
    <t s="24">even higher than the Supernal Man,</t>
    <t s="25">the level of Tikkun.</t>
    <t s="26">And therefore, specifically through them does man live,</t>
    <t s="27">the man below,</t>
    <t s="28">and</t>
    <t s="29">(through this)</t>
    <t s="30">the Supernal Man, as it were.</t>
    <t s="31">And to hint at another matter in this,</t>
    <t s="32">explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="33">at length, the difference between the World of Tikkun and the World of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="34">that both were brought into being by the Supernal Will,</t>
    <t s="35">except that in the World of Tikkun it is in the manner of “this law pleased Me,”</t>
    <t s="36">and in the World of Tohu it is in the manner of “this law did not please Me.”</t>
    <t s="37">That is,</t>
    <t s="38">in the World of Tohu there is the Supernal Will,</t>
    <t s="39">but it is in concealment and hiding,</t>
    <t s="40">while what is revealed is the matter of the opposite of the Will, “this law did not please Me.”</t>
    <t s="41">And therefore, from this descends below,</t>
    <t s="42">that the matters that came into being from the World of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="43">although in revelation they are matters opposite to holiness, “this law did not please Me,”</t>
    <t s="44">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="45">even within them there are sparks of holiness,</t>
    <t s="46">and on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="47">specifically within them there is the intensity</t>
    <t s="48">of the lights of Tohu.</t>
    <t s="49">And this is why through the descent of the soul below it is elevated to a level higher than it was before its descent,</t>
    <t s="50">for this is from the side of the refinements of the sparks of the World of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="51">through which one inherits the lights of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="52">which is the matter of “an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that negative commandments refine even higher sparks than positive commandments, because their fall is greater, and that repentance transforms sins into merits, drawing an incomparably higher light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And so,</t>
    <t s="2">according to the above rule that whatever is higher falls lower, we must say,</t>
    <t s="3">that even within the sparks of Tohu themselves,</t>
    <t s="4">whatever fell lower has its source from a higher place.</t>
    <t s="5">From this it is understood that there is an advantage in the refinements achieved through negative commandments over the refinements of positive commandments,</t>
    <t s="6">for even though the sparks within physical things through which one fulfills a positive commandment also have their source in the World of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="7">nevertheless, the fall within them is not as great,</t>
    <t s="8">since they are permitted matters that are sustained by us.</t>
    <t s="9">However, with negative commandments,</t>
    <t s="10">which involve matters that are forbidden and bound in the hands of the external forces,</t>
    <t s="11">this itself is proof that the source of the sparks clothed within them is higher.</t>
    <t s="12">Therefore, through the service of negative commandments,</t>
    <t s="13">even at the beginning of service when one does not transform willful sins into merits but only pushes them away,</t>
    <t s="14">a more elevated light is drawn down than in the service of positive commandments.</t>
    <t s="15">And as explained in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">positive commandments correspond to Vav-Hei,</t>
    <t s="17">the level of “the revealed things,”</t>
    <t s="18">and negative commandments correspond to Yud-Hei,</t>
    <t s="19">the level of “the hidden things are for G-d”</t>
    <t s="20">(and also – Yud-Hei is a holy Name in itself),</t>
    <t s="21">and the difference between them is an incomparable difference.</t>
    <t s="22">And in general, it is the difference between internal light and encompassing light,</t>
    <t s="23">for positive commandments draw down internal light, which is light that is clothed in vessels,</t>
    <t s="24">while negative commandments draw down encompassing light, which the vessel cannot contain.</t>
    <t s="25">And this advantage of negative commandments over positive commandments exists even when the service in matters of negative commandments is only in the manner of pushing away.</t>
    <t s="26">And certainly when the service in them is in the manner of transforming willful sins into merits,</t>
    <t s="27">then one draws down a light that is incomparably higher even than the light drawn down through negative commandments in the manner of pushing away.</t>
    <t s="28">And it is understood from this that this matter of “willful sins become for him like merits” is only through the service of repentance,</t>
    <t s="29">for the regular service</t>
    <t s="30">(the continual offerings in their order)</t>
    <t s="31">in forbidden matters is only in the manner of pushing away.</t>
    <t s="32">And the difference between these two types of service is an incomparable difference,</t>
    <t s="33">as is understood from every place,</t>
    <t s="34">that the difference between them is like the value of the limited relative to the unlimited.</t>
    <t s="35">And as it is in the matter of time,</t>
    <t s="36">that the service of repentance is “in one hour and in one moment,”</t>
    <t s="37">above the measurement of time,</t>
    <t s="38">whereas regular service is measured in the continuum and expanse of time</t>
    <t s="39">(and consequently also in place).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
